correctness.rationale: The count h is the first equality of consecutive induced world sets, so it counts strict deletions, including deletion to the absorbing empty set. With no letters, induction on syntax and reflexivity make every formula truth-constant, and ⊥ attains one deletion. In the one-agent case each original class evolves without interacting with other classes. Structural induction shows that truth depends only on a world's Boolean valuation type and the current set of types in its class: a diamond amounts to existence of a witnessing type in that set. Each changing round deletes whole types. Once one class has a no-change round it stays fixed, independently of other classes. All classes are therefore fixed after at most 2^k rounds, even on infinite carriers. A single equivalence class containing every valuation type, with the announced test 'some larger type remains', loses exactly one type per round until empty, attaining 2^k. For at least two agents, on an alternating even/odd path with a-pairs (0,1),(2,3),… and b-pairs (1,2),(3,4),… the one-letter formula selects an even world's a-partner or an odd world's b-partner of the opposite valuation. In both cases the required partner is its successor if present. Exactly the rightmost world dies on every nonempty prefix, so n worlds give n strict rounds, including n=1. Extra identity agents do not change the result.
residual_risks: Scope is ordinary truthful world deletion with a fixed static formula, no common knowledge, and empty outcome absorbing. Finite checker cases supplement but do not establish infinite-carrier or unbounded statements.

evidence: The K45 successor-set lemma already counts valuation-type loss with bound 2^|P|. Miller–Moss uses muddy children to exhibit arbitrarily many PAL rounds, with one letter per child. Sadzik considers a wider event-update framework and includes public announcement as a special event.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The type-count mechanism applies to S5 live classes as well and supplies the one-agent upper-bound idea, not the attaining family. Unboundedness with growing resources does not prove unboundedness at fixed agents and alphabet. A general event-update setup does not give the sharp K-dependent numerical classification by specialization alone.

evidence: Yamada's type elimination supplies at most 2^k strict decreases; its D-using proof obtains rank peeling via believed K45 updates with additional formulas. The later ordinary-announcement record attains unbounded rank with a different formula.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Even crediting the one-agent upper bound by transfer of live successor sets, prior upper bounds do not produce matching one-agent sharpness. The known formula in the prior K45 construction does not by a change of notation supply the depth-one fixed-formula S5 path witness; classes must be equivalence relations initially and the test must work on every surviving prefix. The later pair-path theorem illustrates the precise construction overlap, not historical priority.
searches: arXiv:2609.24006v1, Lemmas 6 and 7 and rank-peeling passage

evidence: Yamada's D is exactly the frozen χ up to renaming its letter; its inspected rank proof uses believed announcements on a K45 construction and additional formulas. The later S5 believed-announcement record uses the same formula and alternating-pair path.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In an initially S5 arrow-update model, live targets after t rounds are the intersection of all earlier truth sets. At live worlds every successor is live, and formula truth equals that in the world-induced model by induction. Thus the later identical-path result is a material equivalent construction on the live submodel; it is not pre-record evidence. Yamada's K45 rank proof as stated does not produce that S5 construction. Pointed arrow ranks and global world-set stabilization are not the same invariant on general frames.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The later fixed-formula result independently covers unboundedness at two agents and one bit, not the whole alphabet spectrum. The earlier size bound depends on carrier size and cannot establish a bound uniform in that size. No separate earlier exact entry for the joint invariant was verified.

originality.rationale: Supported for the exact joint agent–alphabet spectrum for ordinary truthful announcement, including sharp one-agent attainability and the depth-one two-agent S5 construction under these semantics. Not new in isolation are the valuation-type upper-bound mechanism, the alternating one-letter formula, or unbounded announcement lifetimes with growing alphabets. The nearest antecedent uses the identical formula and a type-count analogue under believed K45 updates; the comparison of surviving induced structures below shows the connection is more than a keyword match, but does not yield the sharp spectrum from those prior statements.
residual_risks: The focused external web query did not return; not treated as negative evidence. Primary cited passages and named catalogue matches were inspected.
Priority over every possible earlier presentation under iterative relativization or live-target terminology was not established.

value.rationale: The classification asks whether fixing expressive resources alone bounds the duration of a repeated update. It identifies a sharp exponential ceiling independent of carrier size for one agent, versus no ceiling for a fixed depth-one one-letter formula and just two agents. This distinguishes loss of valuation types inside an equivalence class from propagation across two overlapping partitions, with matching examples for the exact ordinary world-deletion convention.
residual_risks: No analogous claim for richer dynamic/event languages or alternative conventions that forbid an empty last round.
